summary: MESH-Harness splits an agent harness into functional slots with fixed interfaces, keeps a pool of LLM-written implementations per slot, uses full-covariance LinUCB over module embeddings to choose which combination to evaluate next, and uses validation traces to have an LLM edit modules. Under a 40-evaluation budget it beats Meta-Harness and four other harness optimizers on text classification, retrieval-augmented math, LiveCodeBench, and ScienceWorld, with lower search and test cost.

claims.claim: Outperforms Meta-Harness by 5.70, 7.01, 2.00, 5.00 points on Text, Math, LiveCodeBench, ScienceWorld under matched 40-evaluation budgets.
claims.evidence: Table 1 numbers match abstract. Test sets small (Table 9: LiveCodeBench 100 problems so +2.00 = 2 problems; USPTO 100, LawBench 100, ScienceWorld 102 episodes). Scores average three test runs of one frozen harness; no variance across search runs or seeds reported.

claims.claim: Both bandit selection and trace-driven module evolution contribute.
claims.evidence: Tables 4-5 (text only): random composition 48.80, alpha=0 51.70, full 56.33; no pool refresh 51.20, refresh without traces 53.80. Single runs, text tasks only.

claims.claim: Test-time cost 44.2% lower and total search+test cost 14.6% lower than Meta-Harness.
claims.evidence: Table 6: $3.5528 -> $1.9835 test-only; $195.0537 -> $166.6078 search+test. Test-only savings dominated by ScienceWorld (59.5%); Text only 2.8%.

claims.claim: Optimized harness transfers across execution models.
claims.evidence: Table 7: frozen text harness keeps 4.36-5.70 point lead with GPT-5.6 Luna, Qwen 3.8 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5. Text tasks only.

patterns.note: Searched/self-improving harness with held-out frozen test evaluation; gains of 5.63-7.79 over first-round configurations.
Validation traces drive module edits; refresh without traces loses 2.53 points (Table 5).
Explicit candidate-evaluation budget and USD cost reporting for search and test.
LiveCodeBench harness uses public examples to test/repair before private scoring.
Evaluation entirely on public benchmarks; no SE repository tasks.

methodology.sample: Six datasets in four domains; test sizes 100-500 instances (Table 9); 40 candidate evaluations per task.
methodology.baselines: SkillOpt, DGM-H, ADIAS, AHE, Meta-Harness (current 2026 harness optimizers) plus fixed reference harnesses; Meta-Harness initialized from fixed harnesses while MESH starts from LLM-generated pools (different initialization).
methodology.models: Optimizer: Claude Code with Claude Opus 5; executor: DeepSeek V4 Flash; transfer to GPT-5.6 Luna, Qwen 3.8 Flash, Claude Sonnet 5.
methodology.variance: Means over three test executions of one frozen harness; no std/CI; single search run per method.
methodology.ablations: Selection rule (alpha sweep, random), pool refresh, trace access - text tasks only.
methodology.contamination_controls: Math retrieval corpus filtered against evaluation questions and deduplicated; LiveCodeBench v6 split; validation/test disjoint.
methodology.languages: Python programs for LiveCodeBench; harness code in Python; other tasks are text/QA.

standards.artifacts: No code link found; reproducibility statement points to algorithm descriptions and appendices only.

biases.detail: One search run per method; only three test re-executions averaged; no CIs on 2-11 point differences.
LiveCodeBench +2.00 on 100 problems is 2 problems; text tests of 100-212 items.
No code or selected-harness release found.
Benchmarks are single-turn classification/QA, competitive programming, and simulated science; no repository-level software engineering.
Authors run all baselines themselves under their budget protocol; no independent replication.

coi.affiliations: CUHK-Shenzhen, CUHK, NTU, Fudan, NUS, and DeepWisdom (company; Chenglin Wu listed).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None of the compared baselines appear to be authors' products; related MASPOB (Hong et al. 2026) shares authors but is not a reported baseline.
coi.detail: One industry affiliation (DeepWisdom) without a product evaluated; usual method-author self-evaluation.

verdict_reason: Numbers in the abstract are supported by tables with current baselines and cost reporting, but single search runs, no variance, small test sets, no artifacts, and no SE-repository tasks limit confidence.
applicability: Moderately useful as a design pattern rather than a tool: structuring the team's harness into slots with fixed interfaces (context builder, retrieval, verifier, recovery) makes components swappable per agent host and lets a small evaluation budget compare variants. A Java team could adopt the discipline (frozen held-out eval set per ingestion workflow, budget-capped search, trace-driven edits) without the bandit machinery. The evidence does not cover multi-repo Java code changes, spec-driven workflows, or domain content; self-modifying harnesses also need tamper auditing before use on regulated content.

conflicts_with.detail: Harness-tampering audit argues self-improving harness gains can be illusory or violate integrity constraints; MESH reports gains without auditing edits, though it uses frozen held-out tests.
Reports self-authored verification is unreliable in self-improving agents; MESH relies on validation-set scores chosen by the optimizer, mitigated only by a frozen held-out test.
